abstract: This CESifo working paper by Althoff and Reichardt investigates how task-specific technical change affects comparative advantage in labor markets. The study examines the relationship between technological innovation targeted at specific job tasks and how this reshapes wage patterns and worker earnings across occupations. The research finds that task-specific technical change can raise average wages by 21 percent, indicating substantial positive labor market effects from technology adoption.
keyFindings: Task-specific technical change raises average wages by 21 percent
Technology adoption impacts comparative advantage across different occupational tasks
Technical change targeted at specific tasks generates significant wage effects rather than uniform labor market impacts
